text.p: The Turkish lira eased to 92,520 per dollar on Friday from 92,415 at Thursday's close on banks' dollar demand.
The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers at 92,375 lira at the opening, up from 92,300 at Thursday's close. During the day, it raised the rate to 92,400 lira.
Bankers said banks' dollar demand was relatively high despite a cash shortage.
September inflation figures had little impact on currency rates.
Wholesale prices rose 5.1 percent in September, up from 3.8 percent a month ago, while consumer prices gained 6.1 percent from 4.8 percent in August.
Bankers said cash demand was strong as banks repaid the central bank a total of 34.2 trillion lira from overnight dealings and repos.

The central bank injected a total of 30.62 trillion lira. Of that, 6.82 trillion lira was injected by buying seven-day repos at an average annual rate of 74.64 percent in an open market auction and 23.8 trillion lira via overnight lending at 75 percent on the interbank.
T-bill yields eased about one point after the price data.
The average yield on the most heavily traded May 7 paper eased to 127.97 percent from 129.09 on Thursday.
The second most active March 26 paper yielded 125.10 percent average, up from 126.58 Thursday average.
